# @quartz-community/obsidian-plugin-excalidraw

A page type plugin that renders [Obsidian Excalidraw](https://github.com/zsviczian/obsidian-excalidraw-plugin) drawings (`.excalidraw.md` and `.excalidraw` files) as full-page interactive SVG visualizations. Supports shapes, text, arrows, freedraw strokes, embedded notes with transcluded content, embedded webpages via iframe, and full dark/light theme adaptation using Excalidraw's color palette.

## Installation

```bash
npx quartz plugin add github:quartz-community/obsidian-plugin-excalidraw
```

## Usage

```yaml title="quartz.config.yaml"
plugins:
  - source: github:quartz-community/obsidian-plugin-excalidraw
    enabled: true
    options:
      enableInteraction: true
      darkMode: "auto"
      exportPadding: 20
```

For advanced use cases, you can override in TypeScript:

```ts title="quartz.ts (override)"
import * as ExternalPlugin from "./.quartz/plugins";

ExternalPlugin.ExcalidrawPage({
  enableInteraction: true,
  darkMode: "auto",
  exportPadding: 20,
});
```

## Features

- **Shapes**: Rectangles, ellipses, and diamonds rendered with roughjs hand-drawn style, respecting fill styles (hachure, cross-hatch, solid), stroke styles (solid, dashed, dotted), and roughness levels.
- **Text**: Multi-line text with Virgil (hand-drawn), Helvetica, and Cascadia font families. Supports alignment and vertical positioning.
- **Arrows and lines**: Smooth curved paths for multi-point arrows with arrowhead markers. Straight lines for two-point connections.
- **Freedraw**: Freeform strokes rendered via perfect-freehand with pressure simulation.
- **Images**: Embedded images displayed from base64 data URLs stored in the drawing.
- **Embedded notes**: Obsidian wikilink embeds (`[[note]]`) resolved and transcluded with rendered HTML content.
- **Embedded webpages**: URL embeds rendered as sandboxed iframes with title bars.
- **Dark/light mode**: Full theme support using CSS custom properties. All 65 Excalidraw palette colors have pre-computed dark-mode equivalents matching Excalidraw's own `applyDarkModeFilter` algorithm.
- **Pan and zoom**: Mouse drag to pan, scroll wheel to zoom, with zoom in/out/reset buttons.
- **Full-viewport layout**: Dedicated page frame with toggleable sidebar (matching canvas-page pattern).
- **Compressed JSON**: Supports both `json` and `compressed-json` (LZ-String) formats from the Obsidian Excalidraw plugin.
- **Filter integration**: Prevents `.excalidraw.md` files from being double-processed as regular Markdown pages.

## Configuration

| Option              | Type      | Default  | Description                                                |
| ------------------- | --------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enableInteraction` | `boolean` | `true`   | Whether to enable pan and zoom interaction on the drawing. |
| `darkMode`          | `string`  | `"auto"` | Theme mode: `"auto"`, `"light"`, or `"dark"`.              |
| `exportPadding`     | `number`  | `20`     | Padding around the drawing content in pixels.              |

## Supported file formats

### `.excalidraw.md` (Obsidian format)

The primary format produced by the [Obsidian Excalidraw plugin](https://github.com/zsviczian/obsidian-excalidraw-plugin). Contains YAML frontmatter, text elements section, optional embedded files section, and the drawing data in a `%%`-delimited block as either `json` or `compressed-json` (LZ-String base64).

### `.excalidraw` (Pure JSON)

Standard Excalidraw JSON format with `type`, `version`, `elements`, `appState`, and `files` fields.

MIT

# quartz-betterbases

Obsidian Bases (`.base` files and `base` code blocks) for [Quartz](https://quartz.jzhao.xyz) v5.

This is a fork of [`@quartz-community/bases-page`](https://github.com/quartz-community/bases-page)
1.0.0 (upstream commit `5c729d1`). Version 0.1.0 only renames the plugin; its behaviour is
identical to upstream. Fixes and features follow in later versions — see `CHANGELOG.md`.

The plugin is for personal use and not published to npm. Install it from its (private) GitHub
repository, which needs access to it:

```bash
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-betterbases
```

`npx quartz plugin update quartz-betterbases` fetches the newest commit of `main`.

Disable `@quartz-community/bases-page` in the same project: both plugins handle the same `.base`
files and `base` code blocks.

## Options added by this fork

| Option                | Default | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `includeVirtualPages` | `false` | Pages without a source file (folder, tag, base and canvas pages) can be entries of a base. Obsidian does not know them.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `listBasePages`       | `false` | The page generated for each `.base` file is listed in search, graph, explorer, sitemap, RSS, backlinks and folder/tag pages. Off, it is marked `unlisted` and stays reachable by URL and links. Embedding a base works either way.                                                                                             |
| `language`            | `auto`  | With quartz-multilanguage: `auto` lists only entries in the language of the page the base is on (untranslated notes are left out), `all` lists every language, a code (`de`) always that one. For different column or view names per language, use one `.base` file per language folder.                                       |
| `search`              | `auto`  | A search field above each view that filters its entries in the browser. `auto` shows it from 8 entries on, `always`, `never`. Searches only the entries on the page, not what `limit` cut off. A custom view gets the field only when it marks its entries with `data-bases-entry`.                                            |
| `showMore`            | `50`    | How many entries a table, cards, list or gallery view shows before a "Show more" button (in a grouped view: each group); a board shows every card, its columns scroll. The rest is on the page: search and sorting reach it, summaries and counts include it. `0` shows everything, like Obsidian, whose views scroll instead. |
| `tagCase`             | `lower` | How lists of tags are shown: `lower`, `upper` or `capitalize` (`#Gross/Klein`). Display only; formulas see lowercase values.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

`file.lang` is the language code quartz-multilanguage detected for a note (`de`, empty without
it), for filters of your own such as `file.lang == this.file.lang`. Obsidian does not know it: a
base that filters on it finds nothing there. The `language` option needs no change to the base.

`file.embeds` lists the notes and bases a note embeds, as paths. Embedded images are missing:
Quartz renders `![[bild.png]]` as an image without a mark that tells it from `![](bild.png)`,
where Obsidian lists both, as links.

## Tags

Tags compare like in Obsidian: `file.tags.contains("a")`, `containsAny`, `containsAll` and
`file.hasTag()` ignore case, accept the tag with or without `#` and match nested tags (`a` matches
`#a/b/c`, not `#ab`). Tag values carry `#`. Two differences remain, both because Quartz has
changed the tags before the plugin sees them: they are lowercased (`#Gross/Klein` becomes
`#gross/klein`; `tagCase` shows them as `#GROSS/KLEIN` or `#Gross/Klein`), and inline tags are merged into the `tags` property, so
`note.tags` also lists tags written in the text, where Obsidian has no `tags` property.

## Linking to a view

The page of a `.base` file opens with its first view, as in Obsidian, and keeps the view you pick
in the address (`x.base#second-table`), so a reload or a shared link shows that view. A link from
a note works the same way: `[[x.base#Second Table]]` opens the base on that view, as it does in
Obsidian. The anchor is what Quartz makes of the view's name in such a link: lower case, spaces
as `-`, punctuation dropped (`Notes: open!` becomes `#notes-open`). An anchor that names no view
shows the first one. Picking a view replaces the address instead of adding a step, so Back leaves
the page. A base embedded in a note switches views without touching the address, since a note
can embed several.

## Dev server: embedded bases can be out of date

`npx quartz build --serve` rebuilds only the notes you changed. A base embedded in a note
(`![[x.base]]`) or written as a `base` code block depends on every note, but Quartz does not know
that, so the note keeps its old rendering:

| Change                               | Page of the `.base` file | Base embedded in a note |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------------- |
| The `.base` file                     | up to date               | out of date             |
| A note the base lists (new, changed) | up to date               | out of date             |
| The note that embeds the base        | up to date               | up to date              |

To refresh, save the note that embeds the base, or restart the dev server. A full build
(`npx quartz build`) is always up to date. The plugin cannot fix this on its own: Quartz gives
plugins no way to re-emit other pages, and touching the embedding notes would change their
modification time in the vault.

# Upstream README: @quartz-community/bases-page

A page type and component plugin for Quartz v5 that renders Obsidian Bases (.base files) as database-like filtered views. This plugin (v0.2.0) provides a powerful way to visualize and interact with your Obsidian data in a structured format.

## Installation

```bash
npx quartz plugin add github:quartz-community/bases-page
```

## Usage

Enable the plugin in your Quartz configuration:

```yaml title="quartz.config.yaml"
plugins:
  - source: github:quartz-community/bases-page
    enabled: true
```

## Interaction with `unlisted` pages

`bases-page` respects the `file.data.unlisted` convention. Pages marked `unlisted: true` (by `@quartz-community/unlisted-pages`, or by `@quartz-community/encrypted-pages` via `unlistWhenEncrypted: true` or per-page `unlisted: true` / `stealth: true`) are excluded from every rendered base view — table, list, board, cards, gallery, and any custom view registered via `viewRegistry`. Both the main entry loop and the internal `fileLookup` used by `.asFile()` method resolution skip unlisted pages, so they cannot be dereferenced from formulas on visible pages either.

> [!note]
> Base views are **server-side rendered** HTML baked at build time. They do not update client-side after a visitor successfully decrypts an encrypted page. Graph, explorer, and search all re-hydrate from the patched in-memory content index after decryption and show newly-unlocked pages for the rest of the browser session — base views do not, because they were materialized at build time with unlisted pages already excluded. A visitor who decrypts a revealable encrypted page will see it appear in graph, explorer, and search, but **not** in any base view on the site, until the site is rebuilt with that page listed. This is the same structural limitation that applies to backlinks, recent notes, folder listings, and tag listings.

### TypeScript Override

For advanced use cases (e.g. custom view renderers), you can override in TypeScript:

```ts title="quartz.ts (override)"
import * as ExternalPlugin from "./.quartz/plugins";

ExternalPlugin.BasesPage({
  defaultViewType: "table",
  linkResolution: "shortest",
  customViews: {
    myView: ({
      entries,
      view,
      basesData,
      total,
      locale,
      slug,
      allSlugs,
      linkResolution,
      options,
    }) => {
      // return JSX
    },
  },
});
```

## Built-in Views

- **Table**: Sortable columns with automatic type rendering for strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, and links. Supports custom column widths and row heights.
- **List**: A compact list view displaying metadata chips for each entry.
- **Cards**: A card-based layout with support for an optional image property and configurable card size or aspect ratio.
- **Gallery**: An image-focused grid layout designed for visual content with configurable card sizes.
- **Board**: A Kanban-style board that groups entries by a specific property (using boardProperty or groupBy), creating columns for each group value.

## Features

- Multiple views per .base file (switchable tabs)
- Recursive filter trees (and/or/not)
- Formulas (computed properties via expression engine)
- Summaries (column aggregations: Count, Average, Min, Max, Sum, Range, Median, Stddev, Earliest, Latest, Checked, Unchecked, Empty, Filled, Unique)
- Property display configuration
- Wikilink and Markdown link rendering
- Sort and grouping

## Expression Engine

The expression engine follows a pipeline of source, lexer, Pratt parser, AST, bytecode compiler, and stack interpreter.

### Supported Types

- Strings
- Numbers
- Booleans
- Null
- Lists

### Operators

- **Arithmetic**: +, -, \*, /; a date plus or minus duration text, as in Obsidian
  (`today() - "30d"`, `now() + "1 week"`: one whole number and one of `y`, `M`, `w`, `d`, `h`,
  `m`, `s` or their words, case-sensitive)
- **Comparison**: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=
- **Logical**: and / &&, or / ||, not / !

### Property Access

- `note.property`: Access a property on the current note.
- `file.name`: The name of the file.
- `file.path`: The full path of the file.
- `file.folder`: The folder containing the file.
- `file.ext`: The file extension.
- `file.tags`: A list of tags associated with the file.
- `file.links`: A list of links in the file.
- `file.backlinks`: The notes that link to the file, in path order.
- `file.created`: The creation date of the file.
- `file.modified`: The last modification date of the file.
- `formula.name`: Access the result of another formula.
- `this`: The page the base is shown on: the note that embeds it, or the base file itself on the
  page of a `.base` file (as in Obsidian when the base is opened on its own). `this.x` is that
  page's property `x`, `this.file` its file (`this.file.name` is `e` for a note `e.md`, `s.base`
  for a base).

### Built-in Global Functions

- `if(condition, then, else)`
- `contains(container, item)`
- `date(string)`: ISO text only (`2024-03-10`, `2024-03-10 14:30`, `20240310`), as in Obsidian
- `duration(string)`: a duration, shown in words ("7 days"); `date - date` is one too. Read its
  length with `.milliseconds`, `.seconds`, `.minutes`, `.hours`, `.days`, `.weeks`, `.months` or
  `.years`
- `now()`
- `today()`
- `number(value)`
- `min(a, b, ...)`
- `max(a, b, ...)`
- `list(value)`
- `link(path, display?)`
- `image(url)`
- `icon(name)`
- `html(string)`
- `escapeHTML(string)`
- `file(path)`

### Method Functions

**Strings**

- `contains(substring)`
- `startsWith(prefix)`
- `endsWith(suffix)`
- `lower()`
- `upper()`
- `trim()`
- `replace(pattern, replacement)`
- `slice(start, end?)`
- `isEmpty()`
- `repeat(count)`
- `reverse()`

**Numbers**

- `toFixed(digits)`
- `round()`
- `floor()`
- `ceil()`
- `abs()`

**Dates**

- `format(formatString)`
- `year()`
- `month()`
- `day()`
- `time()`
- `relative()`
- `isEmpty()`

**Lists**

- `sum()`
- `mean()`
- `count()`
- `min()`
- `max()`
- `round()`

**File**

- `hasTag(tag)`
- `hasLink(link)`
- `inFolder(folder)`
- `hasProperty(property)`

**Links**

- `asFile()`: the note the link names
- `linksTo(file)`: whether the link points to `file` (as Obsidian computes it; a link to a heading
  does not count)

## Extending with Custom Views

Community extensions can register custom view types using the view registry.

### Registering a View

```typescript
import { viewRegistry } from "@quartz-community/bases-page/registry";

viewRegistry.register({
  id: "my-custom-view",
  name: "My Custom View",
  icon: "star",
  render: (props) => {
    const { entries, view, basesData, total, locale, slug, allSlugs, linkResolution, options } =
      props;
    // Return your React/Preact component
  },
  css: `.my-custom-view { color: red; }`,
  afterDOMLoaded: `console.log("My custom view loaded");`,
  options: { enableFeatureX: true },
});
```

### Interfaces

**ViewTypeRegistration**

```typescript
interface ViewTypeRegistration {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  icon?: string;
  render: ViewRenderer;
  css?: string;
  afterDOMLoaded?: string;
  options?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

**ViewRendererProps**

```typescript
interface ViewRendererProps {
  entries: BasesEntry[];
  view: BasesView;
  basesData: BasesData;
  total: number;
  locale: string;
  slug: string;
  allSlugs: string[];
  linkResolution: "absolute" | "relative" | "shortest";
  options?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

### Passing Options to a Custom View

Community plugins can use the `options` field to accept configuration at registration time. This is useful for feature flags, API keys, or other plugin-level settings.

```typescript
import { viewRegistry } from "@quartz-community/bases-page/registry";
import type { LeafletMapPluginOptions } from "./types";

const defaultOptions: LeafletMapPluginOptions = {
  enableCopyTool: false,
};

export function registerLeafletMap(userOpts?: Partial<LeafletMapPluginOptions>): void {
  const opts = { ...defaultOptions, ...userOpts };
  viewRegistry.register({
    ...leafletMapViewRegistration,
    options: opts,
  });
}
```

In the renderer, these options are available via `props.options` and should be cast to the plugin's options type.

## Compiler API

The expression engine is available as a public API for advanced usage. Import from `@quartz-community/bases-page/compiler`.

```typescript
import {
  compile,
  evaluate,
  evaluateFilter,
  resolvePropertyValue,
} from "@quartz-community/bases-page/compiler";

// Compile an expression to bytecode
const compiled = compile("note.price * 1.2");

// Evaluate an expression in a context
const result = evaluate("note.price * 1.2", context);

// Evaluate a filter node
const isMatch = evaluateFilter(filterNode, context);

// Resolve a property path
const value = resolvePropertyValue("file.name", context);
```

### EvalContext Shape

```typescript
interface EvalContext {
  note: Record<string, unknown>;
  file: {
    name: string;
    path: string;
    folder: string;
    ext: string;
    tags: string[];
    links: string[];
    created?: string;
    modified?: string;
  };
  formula: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

## Package Exports

- `.`: Main plugin entry (BasesPage, BasesBody, viewRegistry, registerCustomViews, compiler API, types)
- `./types`: All type definitions
- `./components`: React/Preact components (BasesBody, ViewSelector)
- `./registry`: View registry singleton and registerCustomViews helper
- `./compiler`: Expression engine (compile, evaluate, evaluateFilter, resolvePropertyValue)

## Configuration Options

| Option            | Type                                     | Default      | Description                                                                                    |
| :---------------- | :--------------------------------------- | :----------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultViewType` | `string`                                 | `"table"`    | The default view type used when none is specified in the .base file.                           |
| `linkResolution`  | `"absolute" \| "relative" \| "shortest"` | `"shortest"` | How to resolve internal links in view renderers. Should match your crawl-links plugin setting. |
| `customViews`     | `Record<string, ViewRenderer>`           | `{}`         | Custom view renderers provided via TypeScript override.                                        |

# quartz-forms

A [Quartz v5](https://quartz.jzhao.xyz) plugin for web forms on a static site: contact, feedback,
sign-up and survey forms, rendered at build time, validated in the browser, encrypted with OpenPGP
before they leave the page, and sent through a configurable transport.

**Status: 0.6.0.** Measured in a built site and in Chrome; the PHP relay is measured
under `php -S` by the test suite (`test/relay.test.ts`) and sent real mail through all-inkl.com. Reviewed independently seven times, the
third time 0.4.0 as a whole, the fourth 0.4.1 to 0.5.4, the fifth 0.5.5 and 0.5.6, the sixth 0.5.7,
the seventh 0.5.8 and 0.5.9 (see the CHANGELOG); the placeholder hint and the path of “no fields”
in 0.5.10, in 0.5.11 `counters` and `generation` on the ticket and the probe file beside the
counters, in 0.5.12 the relay's question to OPcache before it reads its config, in 0.5.13
the ticket's `counters` and `generation` only for whoever names the generation, in 0.5.14
the second try after a refused proof of work, in 0.5.15 the generation read past OPcache where
`validate_timestamps=0`, and in 0.5.16 the hCaptcha widget rendered on its `onload` are not
reviewed yet. The envelope sender and the relay's page without JavaScript (0.5.16) were read
along with QuartzControl's review of the mail-test fixes (2026-11-04); the switch
`envelopeSender` (0.6.0) came out of that review and is not reviewed itself.

- Forms are defined once in `quartz.config.yaml` (`options.forms`), by id
- A page embeds a form with a ` ```quartz-form ` code block, a `{{form:id}}` placeholder or
  the frontmatter key `form:`; a form can also sit in a layout area on every page
- Field types: text, email, phone, URL, number, date, textarea, select, radio, checkboxes, a single
  checkbox, a scale, a consent checkbox, a hidden value, and a field for the visitor's own public
  PGP key
- Per form: encryption `required`, `optional` or `off`; an anonymous mode without personal data
- Transports: your own relay (a PHP script ships in `relay/php/`), a generic HTTP endpoint,
  presets for form services, `mailto:`, or a demo that sends nothing and shows what would have
  been sent
- Spam protection, all configurable: honeypot and time trap, proof-of-work and rate limiting in
  the relay, Turnstile/hCaptcha
- Labels in several languages, works with quartz-multilanguage

## Installation

```bash
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-forms
```

```yaml
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-forms
    enabled: true
    options:
      forms: {}
```

## Embedding a form

Three ways on a page, one through the layout:

````markdown
```quartz-form
contact
```
````

```markdown
{{form:contact}}
```

```yaml
---
form: contact # or a list: [contact, feedback]; `form: false` hides the layout form here
---
```

```yaml
# quartz.config.yaml: the same form on every page, placed like any component
options:
  layoutForm: feedback
layout:
  position: afterBody
  priority: 20
```

## Options

All options live under `options:` of the plugin entry. A _Text_ is a string or a record by
language code (`{ de: "Name", en: "Name" }`); the page language picks the entry.

| Option           | Type                                  | Default         | Description                                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `forms`          | `Record<id, Form>`                    | `{}`            | The forms, by id (`[a-z0-9-]`). See below.                               |
| `transport`      | `Transport`                           | `{kind: relay}` | Where submissions go; every form may override single fields.             |
| `keys`           | `Record<name, {file} \| {armored}>`   | `{}`            | Public PGP keys: a file relative to the site root, or the armored text.  |
| `spam`           | `Spam`                                | see below       | Spam protection and limits; every form may override single fields.       |
| `frontmatterKey` | `string`                              | `"form"`        | Frontmatter key that embeds a form or hides the layout form (`false`).   |
| `codeBlockLang`  | `string`                              | `"quartz-form"` | Language tag of the code block that embeds a form.                       |
| `layoutForm`     | `string`                              | `""`            | Id of the form placed through this entry's `layout` block. Empty: none.  |
| `language`       | `"auto"` \| code                      | `"auto"`        | Language of the layout form: the page's, or a fixed code.                |
| `texts`          | `Record<locale, Record<key, string>>` | `{}`            | Own wording for the plugin's texts, e.g. `de: { submit: "Abschicken" }`. |

### Form

| Key           | Type                                          | Default             | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `template`    | `contact` \| `feedback` \| `rsvp` \| `survey` | –                   | Start from a built-in field set. Own `fields` replace it entirely.                                                                                     |
| `title`       | Text                                          | –                   | Heading above the form.                                                                                                                                |
| `description` | Text                                          | –                   | A sentence under the heading.                                                                                                                          |
| `submitLabel` | Text                                          | plugin text         | Text of the submit button.                                                                                                                             |
| `fields`      | `Field[]`                                     | –                   | The fields, in order. Required unless `template` is set.                                                                                               |
| `recipient`   | `string`                                      | –                   | Relay: a _name_ the relay maps to an address in its own config. `mailto`: the address.                                                                 |
| `subject`     | Text                                          | title, else form id | Fixed subject line.                                                                                                                                    |
| `transport`   | partial Transport                             | global              | Overrides single transport fields.                                                                                                                     |
| `encryption`  | `{mode, keys?, showFingerprint?}`             | `mode: off`         | `required`: nothing leaves unencrypted (needs JavaScript). `optional`: a ticked toggle the visitor may untick. `keys`: names from `keys`, default all. |
| `anonymous`   | `boolean`                                     | `false`             | See [Anonymous](#anonymous).                                                                                                                           |
| `pageContext` | `boolean`                                     | `false`             | Send the page's title and slug along (feedback). Never for anonymous forms.                                                                            |
| `spam`        | partial Spam                                  | global              | Overrides single spam fields.                                                                                                                          |
| `success`     | `{mode, text?, slug?}`                        | `mode: inline`      | `inline`: a sentence replaces the form. `redirect`: go to the page `slug` (checked at build).                                                          |
| `className`   | `string`                                      | –                   | Extra class(es) next to `quartz-form`.                                                                                                                 |

### Fields

Every field has `type`, `name` (a letter, then letters, digits, `_` or `-`; unique per form) and,
except `hidden` and `consent`, a `label` (Text). Optional on most: `required`, `hint` (Text),
`width` and `showIf` (see below).

| `type`                                                      | Extra keys                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `text`, `email`, `tel`, `url`, `number`, `date`, `textarea` | `placeholder` (Text), `autocomplete`, `pattern`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `rows`, `maxLength` |
| `select`, `radio`, `checkboxes`                             | `options: [{value, label}]`; `layout` (`radio`, `checkboxes`)                              |
| `checkbox`                                                  | –                                                                                          |
| `scale`                                                     | `min`, `max` (integers, at most 21 steps), `minLabel`, `maxLabel`                          |
| `consent`                                                   | `text` (Text), `link`, `linkLabel`; always required                                        |
| `pgpKey`                                                    | the visitor's own public key (pasted or chosen as a file); at most one                     |
| `hidden`                                                    | `value`                                                                                    |
| `pageBreak`                                                 | no `name`; `title` (Text), `showIf`; starts a step, see [Steps](#steps)                    |

The relay sets `Reply-To` to the first filled-in `email` field. With more than one (yours and a
friend's), give the visitor's own `autocomplete: email`: then only such fields count.

A `pattern` is a JavaScript regular expression (the build and the browser read it with `u`), and
the relay applies it with PCRE: write only what both read the same way. The build refuses what no
PCRE2 reads (`\u` escapes, `[^]`, a lookbehind of unlimited length), and `npm run relay:config`
compiles every pattern with the `php` on your machine and stops at one PCRE cannot read, such as a
property name only JavaScript knows (`--skip-pattern-check` writes the config anyway, for a host
whose PCRE is newer than yours). What the host's PCRE still cannot read makes the relay refuse
every value of that field, with the pattern named in the server's error log.

#### Width and arrangement

`width: half` or `third` sets fields side by side; `full`, the default, takes the whole row. The
widths answer to the form's own width, not the window's, so a form in a sidebar is narrow on a
wide screen too: below 32rem a third becomes a half, below 22rem every field takes the whole row.
These two widths are numbers in the stylesheet, since container queries take no custom
properties. `layout: inline` sets the options of a `radio` or `checkboxes` field side by side,
wrapping where they do not fit; on a `select` it has no effect, and the build says so. Container
queries need Chrome 105, Safari 16 or Firefox 110; an older browser shows every field across the
whole row.

#### Conditions

`showIf: { field, equals }` shows a field only while an earlier field has one of the values.
`field` names a `select`, `radio`, `checkboxes`, `checkbox` or `scale` field before it; `equals`
is one value or a list: option values, `yes` for a `checkbox`, the number as a string for a
`scale`. A `checkboxes` field meets it with any one of the values ticked. Conditions may chain,
and a field whose controlling field does not count does not count either. `hidden` and `consent`
fields cannot be conditional (a `consent` field not through its step either, see Steps; a
`hidden` value arrives even from a step that does not count).

A field that does not count is not required, not checked, not sent and not in the mail; a value
posted for it is dropped, not refused. Without JavaScript every field shows: a conditional one
carries no native `required`, a note under it says when it is needed ("Only needed if …"), and
the relay decides.

#### Steps

An entry `{ type: pageBreak, title?, showIf? }` in `fields` starts a step. It stands between
fields, never first, last or twice in a row. With JavaScript one step shows at a time, under "Step
2 of 4: Title": "Next" (and Return in a field) checks only the open step, "Back" goes back without
checking, and a step whose `showIf` does not hold, or none of whose fields counts, is passed over
both ways. Encryption, captcha and the submit button show with the last step. When the relay
refuses a field, the form opens its step. A step's condition applies to each of its fields but a
`hidden` value, so the relay drops them like any conditional field; a `consent` field therefore
cannot stand in a step with a `showIf`, and the build refuses it there, so no message goes without
the consent. Without JavaScript all steps show one after the other, each under its title.

### Transport

| Key      | Values                                                          | Description                                                                                                |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`   | `relay`, `endpoint`, `formspree`, `web3forms`, `mailto`, `demo` | The plugin's PHP relay; any POST URL; two service presets; the mail program; a demonstration.              |
| `url`    | URL, or the service's form id / access key                      | Required for `relay`, `endpoint` and the presets.                                                          |
| `format` | `json` \| `form`                                                | Body encoding for `endpoint`. The relay gets JSON from the script and a plain post without JavaScript.     |
| `extra`  | `Record<string, string>`                                        | Fields sent with every submission to an `endpoint` or a service; the relay, `mailto` and `demo` take none. |

`demo` sends nothing. The form checks what was typed, encrypts it if it encrypts, and shows below
itself the message as the recipient would have read it, with a button to try again. It needs no
`url` and no `recipient`, ignores `success.mode: redirect` and has no target without JavaScript.
It loads no captcha and sets no time trap (`minSeconds`): nothing is sent that either could protect.
It is meant for a site that shows a form without anyone to receive it, such as a handbook on a
host without PHP.

### Spam

| Key                 | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `honeypot`          | `true`   | An invisible field that must stay empty.                                                                                                                                             |
| `minSeconds`        | `3`      | Whole seconds between opening the page and sending, measured by the relay on the script's post; a plain post without JavaScript carries no stamp (see `noScript`). `0` turns it off. |
| `noScript`          | `true`   | Accept plain form posts from browsers without JavaScript; see below.                                                                                                                 |
| `pow`               | `false`  | Proof of work the relay checks, one per message (`relay` only).                                                                                                                      |
| `powDifficulty`     | `16`     | Leading zero bits, 8 to 20. Hashed in a Worker: 16 takes up to a second on a desktop, 18 and more take seconds on a phone (the build says so).                                       |
| `captcha`           | `none`   | `turnstile` or `hcaptcha`; loads that provider's script. Ignored when anonymous: no widget, and the relay asks for no token.                                                         |
| `captchaSiteKey`    | `""`     | The provider's site key; the secret key goes into the relay's `config.php`.                                                                                                          |
| `rateLimitPerHour`  | `60`     | Mails per form and hour the relay sends; refused posts and failed handovers do not count, no addresses (below).                                                                      |
| `maxFieldLength`    | `2000`   | Default length limit of a single-line field.                                                                                                                                         |
| `maxTextareaLength` | `20000`  | Default length limit of a textarea.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `maxKeyLength`      | `16384`  | Length limit of a pasted public key.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `maxBytes`          | `131072` | Size limit of a whole submission, in bytes, measured on its content (a plain post's URL encoding does not count); the build warns when the fields may hold more.                     |

With the relay, the script fetches a ticket when the page opens (`GET send.php?challenge=<id>`):
a stamp of that moment signed by the relay for that form, and the hour's proof-of-work challenge
if the form asks for one. The time trap is measured on that stamp with the relay's clock, so a
visitor's clock that runs ahead does not lock them out, and a made-up stamp or another form's is
refused; a stamp serves its form for a day, so a page left open keeps working. When the relay
does not take the stamp (none came when the page opened, or it is older than a day), the script
fetches a new one, waits `minSeconds` and sends once more; only then does it ask for a reload.
A solved proof of
work sends one message; the relay remembers used ones beside its counters, an hour's worth in a
directory of its own, and marks a proof as used only once the message is accepted and within the
hour's quota, so a refused post does not cost the visitor a new one.
The nonce starts at a random prefix, because the challenge is the same for every visitor of the
hour.

Without JavaScript a form with `encryption: off` or `optional` posts as a plain form to the relay,
which answers with the redirect or a short page (one that names the refused fields with the
sentences the script would show, and after sending links back to the site). Such a post carries neither the stamp nor a
proof of work, so the relay applies only honeypot, rate limit and field checks to it; with
`pow: true` or a `minSeconds` of your own the build says so. `noScript: false` refuses these posts and renders the form without
a target until the script runs, with a `<noscript>` note. With `optional` the "send encrypted" box stays unticked and disabled until the
script enables it, and a `<noscript>` note says the form sends unencrypted; a plain post that
carries the box anyway is refused by the relay.

The rate limit protects your mailbox, not your form. It counts a form's mails per hour, with no
address, so it is one quota for everyone: a single client that sends the hour's mails itself
(60 plain posts take under a second) closes the form to every other visitor until the hour is
over, and you receive those 60. Only a captcha makes each such post cost something, or a proof
of work with `noScript: false`, which a plain post cannot skip; an anonymous form loads no
captcha. Without either the build says so for every relay form.

## Anonymous

`anonymous: true` on a form means, and the code enforces it:

- No required personal field: `email`, `tel`, `pgpKey` and fields whose `autocomplete` names a
  person become optional (the build says so).
- No page context, no `Reply-To`, no third-party captcha (nothing of the visitor goes to a third
  party), and the relay logs nothing.

What it cannot promise: your hoster's access log, the network in between, and what a form
service (`formspree`, `web3forms`) records on its side. The build warns about that combination.

## Encryption

OpenPGP.js runs in the visitor's browser, loaded from `static/quartz-forms/openpgp/` only on
pages that need it. The message (`Label: value` per field, the page, the visitor's key) is
encrypted to the configured public keys; only the armored ciphertext leaves the page, as the
body of the mail. Read it with `gpg`, Thunderbird, Mailvelope or GPG Suite. The fingerprint of the
recipient key is shown under the form so a visitor can compare it with the one you publish.

The build checks every key in use: readable, public, not revoked, not expired, able to encrypt;
it logs the fingerprint and stops on a problem. A key whose encryption subkey is X25519 or X448 in
the form RFC 9580 gave them (what OpenPGP.js 6 creates for `curve25519` and `curve448`) passes, but
GnuPG cannot read it (measured with 2.5.22) and decrypts nothing sent to it; the build says so. The
same holds for any key of version 6 (RFC 9580), whatever its algorithm. A key made with `gpg`
(cv25519, RSA) has no such problem.

Encryption protects the message on its way and in your mailbox, not on the page. Every script on
the page where the visitor types can read the fields before they are encrypted: the captcha
provider's widget (the build says so for an encrypting form with `captcha`), Quartz' `analytics`,
another plugin's script. In the clear travel the form's id, the page's language, the stamp (the
second the page was opened), that the message is encrypted, and the size of the ciphertext; the
mail carries the form's subject and no `Reply-To`, so you answer once you have decrypted the
visitor's address. A service (`endpoint`, `formspree`, `web3forms`) gets the ciphertext as `message`
with the form's `subject` as `_subject`, the transport's `extra` fields and a captcha's token
beside it; the page stays inside the ciphertext.

If OpenPGP.js cannot be loaded in a visitor's browser (network, content blocker, a strict CSP),
an encrypting form says so and sends nothing. A form that does not encrypt still sends; a key the
visitor pasted into a `pgpKey` field then goes out as pasted, checked for its markers only, and
the field says that it went unchecked.

## Validation

The rules of a field stand once, in its definition, and are applied three times: at build time
(ids, names, options, keys, transport, redirect pages), in the browser (with messages in the page
language, on leaving a field and on sending) and in the relay (every plain-text field; an
encrypted submission only by its armor and size). Which fields count under their conditions and
steps is decided the same way in all three: the build holds a condition to an earlier field and
to values it can have, and browser and relay read one list per field derived from it, in one
pass in form order.

## Styling

Every tunable value is a custom property on `.quartz-form`: `--quartz-forms-gap`, `-radius`,
`-border`, `-border-focus`, `-field-bg`, `-error`, `-success`, `-button-bg`, `-button-fg`,
`-max-width`. Set them in `custom.scss`:

```scss
.quartz-form {
  --quartz-forms-button-bg: var(--tertiary);
}
```

The stylesheet sits in Quartz' cascade layer `quartz-base`, so any rule outside it wins whatever
its specificity: your `custom.scss`, and just as much a theme's own unlayered rules. A theme that
styles the article's `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `label`, `button`, `fieldset` or `pre` styles
the form's too (edge, ground, font size, the button's colours). Two rules stand outside the layer
on purpose (`guard.scss`): the form's checkboxes and radios keep the browser's look, and its
paragraphs, headings, fieldsets and the demo's output keep no outer margin; a selector more
specific than `.quartz-form input[type="checkbox"]` or `.quartz-form p` overrides them.

## Texts

Every sentence the plugin shows comes from `src/i18n/locales/` (`en-US`, `de-DE`) and can be
replaced per locale: `texts: { de: { submit: "Abschicken" } }`. Keys are those of `en-US.ts`;
`{name}` placeholders are filled by the code. The German texts and templates address the visitor
informally (du). For the formal Sie, replace the sentences through `texts` and write your own
`fields`; the relay's page for a post without JavaScript keeps its own sentences, which say du.
The message itself is written in the page's language too, including its two lines of the
plugin's own (`messagePage`, `messageKey`); in a mail the relay writes for a post without
JavaScript they are the plugin's defaults, not those from `texts`.

## The relay

`relay/php/` holds a single `send.php` for classic web hosting with PHP 8.1 or newer and its
mbstring extension (the relay says so when that is missing). `npm run relay:config --
/path/to/site` writes its generated configuration from the site's `quartz.config.yaml`; recipient
addresses go into `config.php` by hand and never reach the site. See
[relay/php/README.md](relay/php/README.md).

The same generator ships as a command line for an installed copy (`.quartz/plugins/quartz-forms`
in a site), without `npm install`:

```bash
node dist/cli.js relay --site <site> --out <dir> [--skip-pattern-check] [--json]
node dist/cli.js check --site <site> [--json]   # problems, hints, every key with its fingerprint
node dist/cli.js key   --site <site> --file <key.asc> [--json]
node dist/cli.js texts [--json]                 # the plugin's wording of every text, by locale
```

`--lang de` gives the problems, hints, key problems and refusals in German (English without it;
the build log stays English).

`relay` into a directory of its own writes the whole relay (`send.php`, `counters/.htaccess`,
`counters/qf-probe.count`, `config.generated.php`, `config.php`). With the owner's values as JSON
in the environment variable
`QF_RELAY_OPERATOR` (secret, origins, sender, mailer, envelope sender, recipients, captcha
secrets, counter directory) it writes `config.php` from them on every run; secrets never go through argv. With
`--json` stdout holds one object, among others a `hash` of the generated rules that stays the same
as long as they do, and a `generation` that is new on every run and that the uploaded relay's
ticket answers. This is what QuartzControl runs. `config.php` is written with mode 0600; an
upload over SFTP or FTP does not keep that, so check its mode on the host (see
`relay/php/README.md`, step 3).

The relay answers only requests from the site's origin. A site with `Referrer-Policy:
no-referrer` hides that origin from a plain form post without JavaScript (the browser sends
`Origin: null`), so the relay refuses such posts and says why; the script's requests carry the
origin under any policy.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run check   # typecheck + lint + format + tests
npm run build   # writes dist/ (committed, Quartz installs from it)
```

`dist/` is committed on purpose. After changing anything under `src/`, run `npm run build` and
commit the updated `dist/`.

A German version of this README is in [README.de.md](README.de.md).

# quartz-layout-box A [Quartz v5](https://quartz.jzhao.xyz) component plugin that renders an HTML or Markdown snippet anywhere in the page layout: sidebar, header, footer, before or after the body. Use it for a site title block, a logo, a call-to-action, a notice, or any small piece of static markup you don't want to hard-code into a theme. **📖 The handbook is at [boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/layout-box](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/layout-box/)** — nine chapters in English and German, with every option explained by example, a chapter of recipes, and the reasons behind the awkward parts. This README is the short version. - Snippet from a file (`quartz/static/snippets/` by default) or inline in `quartz.config.yaml` - Markdown snippets (`.md`) are rendered at build time - `{{placeholders}}` for page title, slug, site title, root path and frontmatter values - Optional heading and collapsible `
` box, no client-side JavaScript - Per-page control via frontmatter (hide the box, switch the snippet or the title) - Per-language options (`byLang`) for bilingual sites, keyed on the page's `lang` - Snippet changes are picked up in `quartz build --serve` without a restart - Light/dark image switching via `.img-light` / `.img-dark` ## Installation ```bash npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-layout-box ``` Create the default snippet at `quartz/static/snippets/snippet.html` in your site, then add the plugin to `quartz.config.yaml`: ```yaml plugins: - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-layout-box enabled: true options: file: snippet.html layout: position: left priority: 15 ``` The plugin can be added more than once, with different options and different places — see [Placement](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/3-placement/). ## Options | Option | Type | Default | Description | | ---------------- | --------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `file` | `string` | `"snippet.html"` | Snippet filename inside `dir`. Files ending in `.md` are rendered as Markdown. | | `dir` | `string` | `"quartz/static/snippets"` | Snippet directory, relative to the site root. Files outside it are refused. | | `html` | `string` | – | Inline HTML. Takes precedence over `file`. | | `className` | `string` | – | Extra class(es) added next to the fixed `layout-box` class. | | `title` | `string` | – | Heading (`h3`) rendered above the content. May contain placeholders. | | `collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | Render as `
` with `title` as the summary. Requires `title`. | | `collapsed` | `boolean` | `false` | Start collapsed (only with `collapsible`). | | `placeholders` | `boolean` | `true` | Replace `{{...}}` tokens in the snippet. | | `frontmatterKey` | `string` | `"layoutBox"` | Frontmatter key used for per-page control. | | `byLang` | `object` | – | Per-language overrides, keyed by language code or locale. See below. | An option written without a value (`html:` with nothing after it) counts as not set, in `byLang` as well. Inline HTML example: ```yaml options: title: Note collapsible: true html: |

This site is a work in progress.

``` Everything else — placeholders, per-page control, two languages, styling, error messages and the limits — is in the handbook: | Chapter | | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | [1 Getting started](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/1-getting-started/) | What the plugin is for, your first box, what happens at build time | | [2 The snippet](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/2-the-snippet/) | File or configuration, HTML or Markdown | | [3 Placement](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/3-placement/) | The six places, order, several instances | | [4 Placeholders](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/4-placeholders/) | Every token, and why addresses want `{{root}}` | | [5 Form](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/5-form/) | Heading, collapsing, styling | | [6 Per page](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/6-per-page/) | Hiding and swapping through frontmatter | | [7 Two languages](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/7-two-languages/) | `byLang` | | [8 Recipes](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/8-recipes/) | Finished examples, all of them visible on that site | | [9 Reference](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/layout-box/9-reference/) | Every option, every message, the limits | A German version of this README is in [README.de.md](README.de.md); the handbook is bilingual too. ## Development ```bash npm install npm run check # typecheck + lint + format + tests npm run build # writes dist/ (committed, Quartz installs from it) ``` `dist/` is committed on purpose. After changing anything under `src/`, run `npm run build` and commit the updated `dist/`. ## How this was built A hobby project. The plugin came out of work on [QuartzControl](https://github.com/boxi-os/QuartzControl), but it stands on its own in any Quartz 5 project. One thing I want to be open about: the code was written mostly with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code); the commits say so with a `Co-Authored-By` line. I am aware that vibe coding is a contested subject, and I do not want to hide anything here. ## How well is the code checked? `npm run check` runs the typecheck, the linter, the formatter, 38 tests and the build; CI does the same on every push. That is not a guarantee, but it is something you can run yourself before you trust the plugin. ## License MIT

# quartz-multilanguage

Multilingual content for [Quartz](https://quartz.jzhao.xyz) v5. Quartz itself knows one `locale`
per site; this plugin adds everything needed to publish the same notes in several languages from
one vault.

**📖 The handbook is at [boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/multilanguage](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/multilanguage/)** —
nine chapters in English and German, with every option explained by example and the reasoning behind
the awkward parts. This README is the short version.

- Language detection per page: language folders (`de/…`), file suffixes (`note.de.md`) or a
  frontmatter field, in any priority order
- Linking of translations: explicit (`translationKey`, `translations`), via Obsidian aliases
  (compatible with the Obsidian plugin "Multilingual") or implicitly by identical paths
- A language switcher component: text links, dropdown or flags; labels as code, name, native
  name or the translated page title
- `<html lang>`, `hreflang`/`x-default` links and `og:locale` per page
- Redirect from `/` to a language home, by browser language and remembered choice
- Optional notices ("only available in English" / "also available in German"), fallback
  redirects for missing translations, same-language link rewriting, localized dates
- Publish only some languages (`publishLanguages`, `QUARTZ_LANGS`) for one build per language

## Installation

```bash
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-multilanguage
```

Then add the plugin to `quartz.config.yaml`. One entry configures the transformer, filter,
emitter and the `LanguageSwitcher` component together; `layout` places the switcher.

```yaml
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-multilanguage
    enabled: true
    order: 65 # after crawl-links (60), so link rewriting sees resolved links
    options:
      languages:
        - { code: de, label: German, native: Deutsch, locale: de-DE }
        - { code: en, label: English, native: English, locale: en-US }
      defaultLanguage: en
      rootRedirect: browser
    layout:
      position: header
      group: toolbar
```

`order` only matters for `rewriteCrossLanguageLinks` — see
[7.2](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/7-notices/02-links-between-languages).

## Options

| Option                       | Type                                                 | Default                                  | Description                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `languages`                  | `(string \| Language)[]`                             | `["en"]`                                 | Languages of the site, see below. Strings are codes.                                                               |
| `defaultLanguage`            | `string`                                             | first language                           | Language of pages that match no detection strategy.                                                                |
| `detection`                  | `("folder" \| "suffix" \| "frontmatter")[]`          | all three                                | Detection strategies in priority order. `[]` puts every page in the default language.                              |
| `linking`                    | `("frontmatter" \| "aliases" \| "path")[]`           | all three                                | Linking strategies in priority order.                                                                              |
| `frontmatterKeys`            | `{ lang, key, translations }`                        | `lang`, `translationKey`, `translations` | Frontmatter keys read by the plugin.                                                                               |
| `rootRedirect`               | `"none" \| "default" \| "browser"`                   | `"none"`                                 | Write `index.html` at the site root redirecting to a language home. Only when the vault has no root `index.md`.    |
| `rememberChoice`             | `boolean`                                            | `true`                                   | Store the language chosen in the switcher in `localStorage`; the root redirect honours it.                         |
| `seo.hreflang`               | `boolean`                                            | `true`                                   | `<link rel="alternate" hreflang>` for every translation. Needs `configuration.baseUrl`.                            |
| `seo.ogLocale`               | `boolean`                                            | `true`                                   | `og:locale` and `og:locale:alternate`.                                                                             |
| `seo.xDefault`               | `"default" \| "none" \| <code>`                      | `"default"`                              | Which translation `x-default` points to.                                                                           |
| `switcher.style`             | `"links" \| "dropdown" \| "flags"`                   | `"links"`                                | Appearance of the switcher.                                                                                        |
| `switcher.label`             | `"code" \| "label" \| "native" \| "translatedTitle"` | `"label"`                                | Text of each entry. `translatedTitle` shows the target page's title.                                               |
| `switcher.showCurrent`       | `boolean`                                            | `true`                                   | Show the current language as a highlighted, non-link entry.                                                        |
| `switcher.missing`           | `"hide" \| "home" \| "disabled"`                     | `"home"`                                 | Languages without a translation of the current page: hide, link to their home, or show greyed out.                 |
| `switcher.separator`         | `string`                                             | `"\|"`                                   | Separator between entries in `links` style. Empty string for none.                                                 |
| `switcher.title`             | `string`                                             | translated "Language"                    | Accessible name of the switcher.                                                                                   |
| `missingTranslationNotice`   | `boolean`                                            | `false`                                  | Show "This page is only available in …" when the page has no translation in the visitor's language.                |
| `availableTranslationNotice` | `boolean`                                            | `false`                                  | Show "This page is also available in …" with a link when a translation in the visitor's language exists.           |
| `fallbackPages`              | `"none" \| "redirect"`                               | `"none"`                                 | Write redirect pages where a translation is missing (`de/coffee` → `en/coffee`) for folder and suffix conventions. |
| `rewriteCrossLanguageLinks`  | `boolean`                                            | `false`                                  | Rewrite links that point to another language's page when the same page exists in the page's language.              |
| `localizeDates`              | `boolean`                                            | `false`                                  | Re-format `<time datetime>` elements (content-meta dates) client-side in the page language.                        |
| `publishLanguages`           | `string[]`                                           | `[]` (all)                               | Only publish these languages. `QUARTZ_LANGS=de,en` overrides at build time.                                        |

A language entry:

| Field    | Description                                                                                                           |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`   | Code used in folders, suffixes and frontmatter, e.g. `de`. Required.                                                  |
| `label`  | Display name, e.g. `German`. Defaults to the upper-cased code.                                                        |
| `native` | Name in the language itself, e.g. `Deutsch`. Defaults to `label`. Used for `switcher.label: native` and in notices.   |
| `locale` | BCP 47 locale for `<html lang>`, `hreflang` and `og:locale`, e.g. `de-DE`. Defaults to `code`.                        |
| `home`   | Slug of the language's home page. Defaults to `<code>/index` if it exists, else `index` for the default language.     |
| `flag`   | Text or emoji for `switcher.style: flags`. Defaults to the flag of the locale's region (`de-DE` → 🇩🇪), else the code. |

Defaults live in the plugin code; Quartz passes the raw YAML options through.

Everything else — how content is laid out, how translations find each other, the switcher, SEO,
redirects, notices and building one site per language — is in the handbook:

| Chapter                                                                                           |                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [1 Getting started](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/1-getting-started/) | What Quartz does alone, your first bilingual site, the six parts |
| [2 Detection](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/2-detection/)             | Folder, suffix, frontmatter — and the base path                  |
| [3 Linking](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/3-linking/)                 | `translationKey`, aliases, path, and what to do when it fails    |
| [4 The switcher](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/4-switcher/)           | Shapes, labels, missing translations                             |
| [5 Addresses](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/5-addresses/)             | `hreflang`, `x-default`, `og:locale`, `html lang`                |
| [6 Redirects](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/6-redirects/)             | The start page, fallback pages                                   |
| [7 Notices and links](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/7-notices/)       | The two notices, cross-language links, dates                     |
| [8 Building](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/8-building/)               | One site for all, or one per language                            |
| [9 Reference](https://boxi-os.github.io/quartz-plugins/en/multilanguage/9-reference/)             | Every option, the explorer filter, the limits                    |

A German version of this README is in [README.de.md](README.de.md); the handbook is bilingual too.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run check   # typecheck + lint + format + tests
npm run build   # writes dist/ (committed, Quartz installs from it)
```

`dist/` is committed on purpose. After changing anything under `src/`, run `npm run build` and
commit the updated `dist/`.

## How this was built

A hobby project. The plugin came out of work on
[QuartzControl](https://github.com/boxi-os/QuartzControl), but it stands on its own in any Quartz 5
project.

One thing I want to be open about: the code was written mostly with
[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code); the commits say so with a `Co-Authored-By` line. I
am aware that vibe coding is a contested subject, and I do not want to hide anything here.

## How well is the code checked?

`npm run check` runs the typecheck, the linter, the formatter, 66 tests and the build; CI does
the same on every push. That is not a guarantee, but it is something you can run yourself before you
trust the plugin.

# quartz-navigations

Navigations for [Quartz](https://quartz.jzhao.xyz) v5, built from the folder structure of your
content. One plugin, as many instances as you like: a menu bar in the header, an accordion for the
current section in the sidebar, a sitemap in the footer, previous/next links under the article.
Each instance picks its own levels, sorting and presentation.

- Tree from the content folders at build time, with folder titles from `index.md` or the folder
  name
- Levels and scope per instance: the whole site, one section, the current folder, only siblings
- Ten presentations: `tree`, `bar`, `accordion`, `dropdown`, `flyout`, `tabs`, `mega`, `columns`,
  `select`, `pager`; each one implies its orientation
- Mobile modes per instance: accordion, off-canvas panel with burger, jump menu, hidden
- Sorting: manual (order list in YAML, `navOrder` in frontmatter, numeric file prefixes),
  alphabetical or by date
- `active` on the current page, `active-trail` on every folder above it, `aria-current="page"`
- Whole rows are click targets: a folder row toggles the folder, or is a link with a toggle
  button at its end; submenus open on click or on hover
- Follows the Quartz theme (colors, fonts, dark mode); every value is a `--quartz-nav-*` CSS
  variable you can override from `custom.scss`
- Subtle animations for opening folders, panels and the off-canvas menu, off with
  `prefers-reduced-motion`
- Folder and file glyphs on every row like a file explorer, with sizes and weights stepping
  down by level; per-page icons via `navIcon: lucide:book-open` or `nodeIcons` in the config;
  chevrons, burger and pager arrows are [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) icons too
- Works without JavaScript; the small client script adds remembered folder state, hover menus
  and the scroll lock
- Multilingual sites with quartz-multilanguage: one navigation per page language, whichever way
  the languages are laid out
- Breakpoints are read from your site's `quartz/styles/variables.scss`, not hard-coded

## Installation

```bash
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
```

Then add one entry per navigation to `quartz.config.yaml`. `layout` places the instance; the
plugin can be listed as often as you need. An entry without a `layout` block is not dropped:
Quartz places it at the plugin's default, `left` with `priority: 10`.

```yaml
plugins:
  # Header: the first level as a menu bar, off-canvas panel on phones
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: bar
      depth: 1
      mobile: offcanvas
    layout:
      position: header
      priority: 20

  # Sidebar: the section the current page belongs to, as an accordion
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: accordion
      scope: section
      showScopeRoot: true
      persistState: true
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 20
      display: desktop-only

  # Under the article: previous / next
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: pager
    layout:
      position: afterBody
      priority: 10

  # Footer: a sitemap in columns
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: columns
      depth: 2
    layout:
      position: footer
      priority: 10
```

## How the tree is built

Every page becomes a node; every folder becomes a node whose link is the folder page
(`docs/index`). Quartz's folder-page plugin generates that page when there is no `index.md`, so
folders are always linkable. Titles come from, in this order: the `navTitle` frontmatter key, the
page title, the real directory or file name, the slug segment.

Pages control themselves through frontmatter (keys configurable via `frontmatterKeys`):

| Key        | Effect                                                                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `navOrder` | Number used by `sort: manual`. Lower first. On an `index.md` it orders the folder.   |
| `navTitle` | Title shown in the navigation instead of `title`.                                    |
| `navHide`  | `true` hides the page; on an `index.md` it hides the whole folder.                   |
| `navIcon`  | Icon before the title: `lucide:<name>`, short text, an emoji, or `none` (see Icons). |

Hidden by default: the `tags` folder, `unlisted` pages, drafts and the 404 page.

## Options

| Option                 | Type                                                                                                               | Default                                                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `language`             | `"auto" \| "all" \| string`                                                                                        | `"auto"`                                                                                               | Cooperation with quartz-multilanguage: the tree of the current page's language, `all` for every language, or a fixed language code. See "Multilingual sites".                                                                                            |
| `variant`              | `"tree" \| "bar" \| "accordion" \| "dropdown" \| "flyout" \| "tabs" \| "mega" \| "columns" \| "select" \| "pager"` | `"tree"`                                                                                               | Presentation, see below. Each variant implies its orientation.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `mobile`               | `"same" \| "accordion" \| "offcanvas" \| "select" \| "hidden"`                                                     | `"same"`                                                                                               | Presentation below the mobile breakpoint.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `align`                | `"left" \| "center" \| "right" \| "full"`                                                                          | `"left"`                                                                                               | Alignment of the top row of `bar`, `dropdown`, `mega` and `tabs`; `full` spreads the entries over the whole width. Ignored by the other variants.                                                                                                        |
| `className`            | `string`                                                                                                           | `""`                                                                                                   | Extra classes on the `<nav>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `id`                   | `string`                                                                                                           | hash of the options                                                                                    | Stable instance id for element ids and `localStorage`. Set it when one layout uses the same options twice, otherwise both instances share their element ids.                                                                                             |

With `folderClick: link` the chevron is the toggle button and always shown.                                                                                                                                             |
| `icons`                | `"none" \| "type" \| "custom" \| "both"`                                                                           | `"both"`                                                                                               | `type`: folder and file glyphs. `custom`: `navIcon` / `nodeIcons`. `both`: custom where set, glyph elsewhere. `true` / `false` mean `both` / `none`.                                                                                                     |

Frontmatter wins.                                                                                                                                       |
| `rootPath`             | `string`                                                                                                           | `""` (site root)                                                                                       | Folder the navigation starts at, e.g. `docs` or `de`.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `scope`                | `"root" \| "section" \| "parent" \| "current"`                                                                     | `"root"`                                                                                               | `root`: children of `rootPath`. `section`: the top-level folder of the current page. `parent`: the folder containing the current page (`rootPath` itself on its index page). `current`: the current folder.                                              |
| `depth`                | `number`                                                                                                           | `0` (unlimited)                                                                                        | Levels below the scope root.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| `sort`                 | `"manual" \| "alphabetical" \| "date"`                                                                             | `"manual"`                                                                                             | `manual`: `order` list → `navOrder` → numeric prefix → title. | `sortDirection`        | `"asc" \| "desc"`                                                                                                  | `"asc"`                                                                                                | Missing values (no date, no order) always go last.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `foldersFirst`         | `"first" \| "last" \| "mixed"`                                                                                     | `"first"`                                                                                              | Folders before pages, after them, or sorted together.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
